topic: Extremist Phase and Swadeshi Movement (1905 to 1918)
description: This phase of the Indian National Movement is characterized by the rise of Extremist leaders, mass protests against the Partition of Bengal, and the emergence of revolutionary activities. It marked a shift from moderate petitioning to aggressive strategies like Swadeshi and Boycott.

sections.title: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement
sections.description: The Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon sparked widespread resentment and gave birth to the Swadeshi and Boycott movements, uniting the masses against British rule.

key_concepts.explanation: The promotion and use of indigenous goods and national education to achieve economic self-reliance and reduce dependence on the British.
The complete renunciation of foreign goods, British government services, courts, schools, and official titles as a form of passive resistance.

historical_events.significance: Lord Curzon announced the division of Bengal into two provinces, citing 'administrative convenience' but actually intending to weaken the nationalist nerve center.
The formal proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement was made with the passing of the Boycott resolution at the Calcutta Town Hall.
Observed as a 'Day of Mourning' across Bengal. People fasted, bathed in the Ganga, and marched singing 'Vande Mataram'.

important_facts.fact: On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore, October 16, 1905, was also observed as 'Rakhi Bandhan Day' to symbolize the unbreakable unity between Hindus and Muslims.

sections.title: Rise of Extremism and the Surat Split
sections.description: Ideological clashes over the pace and methods of the Swadeshi movement led to a formal divide between the Moderates and Extremists within the Congress.

key_concepts.explanation: A political approach that rejected the Moderate methods of 'prayers and petitions', advocating instead for direct action, self-sacrifice, and passive resistance to achieve Swaraj.

historical_events.significance: The Indian National Congress formally split into two factions: the Moderates and the Extremists, during the Surat Session presided over by Rashbehari Ghosh.

key_associations.associated_with: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal
key_associations.extra_info: Known as the 'Extremist Trinity', they were the most prominent leaders of the radical nationalist faction.
A book written by Tilak during his 6-year imprisonment in Mandalay Jail (Burma).

important_facts.fact: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the famous slogan: 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it'.

sections.title: First Phase of Revolutionary Activities
sections.description: Following the suppression of the Extremist movement, frustrated youth turned to armed struggle and secret societies to overthrow British rule by force.

historical_events.significance: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage believing it carried the unpopular British judge, Douglas Kingsford.
Aurobindo Ghosh and Barindra Kumar Ghosh, along with others, were put on trial for illegal possession of arms and conspiracy against the Crown.
Founded in San Francisco, USA, by Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and others to organize an armed rebellion in India.

key_associations.associated_with: Pramatha Nath Mitra and Barindra Kumar Ghosh
key_associations.extra_info: The first major revolutionary secret society established in Bengal.
A secret revolutionary organization founded in Maharashtra in 1904.

sections.title: Home Rule League Movement and Lucknow Pact
sections.description: During World War I, the demand for self-government gained momentum, and a brief period of unity emerged in Indian politics.

key_concepts.explanation: The demand for self-government or Dominion Status for India within the British Empire, inspired by the Irish Home Rule movement.

historical_events.significance: Founded in Belgaum, its area of operation was restricted to Maharashtra, Karnataka, Central Provinces, and Berar.
Launched in Madras, it covered the rest of India not included in Tilak's league.
A historic agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League to present joint political demands to the British.

important_facts.fact: The Lucknow Session of 1916, presided over by Ambika Charan Majumdar, also witnessed the reunion of the Moderates and Extremists after 9 years.

sections.title: British Response and Concessions
sections.description: The British government used a 'carrot and stick' policy, combining minor constitutional reforms with severe repressive measures.

historical_events.significance: Introduced 'separate electorates' for Muslims, officially institutionalizing the 'Divide and Rule' policy in Indian politics.
King George V announced the annulment of the Partition of Bengal and the shifting of the British Indian capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
An emergency criminal law enacted during World War I with the primary intention of curtailing nationalist and revolutionary activities.

important_facts.fact: Lord Minto is known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India due to the provisions of the 1909 reforms.
